items.item: A breadcrumb leads back to the contracts list and ends with the contract number, and the header shows the contract number, vendor name, a status badge with text, and at most four key fields (such as value, start and end date)
items.evidence: Breadcrumb 'Contracts / Vendor Agreements / CTR-2024-0317' (nav, lines 42-48) correctly links back and ends with the contract number, and the header shows the status badge ('Active', #status-badge) and exactly 4 key-stat tiles (Total Contract Value, Effective Date, Expiration Date, Days to Renewal Decision). But the header text 'Contract ID: CTR-2024-0317 · Category: IT Infrastructure · Owner: Marcus Reyes, Procurement Lead' (line 60) never names the vendor — 'NorthBridge Networks Inc.' only appears in the separate right-column Vendor card, not the header.

items.item: The header has one primary action (such as "Renew contract") and puts other actions such as edit or terminate in a secondary or overflow position
items.evidence: The only primary-styled (bg-blue-600) header button is `<button id="editBtn">Edit Contract</button>` (line 65); 'Download PDF' and 'Share' are secondary outline buttons. There is no renewal/primary business action in the header, and no terminate action exists anywhere on the page to be demoted to secondary/overflow — Edit itself is the primary action, which is the opposite of what the checklist requires.

items.item: Vendor contacts show each person's name and role, with email as a `mailto:` link and phone as a `tel:` link, and the primary contact is marked with text
items.evidence: Each contact card shows name/role plus links, e.g. 'Sade Okonkwo' / 'Account Manager (Primary)' with `<a href="mailto:s.okonkwo@northbridgenet.com">` and `<a href="tel:+15125550148">` (lines 379-382); the primary contact is explicitly labeled '(Primary)' in text.

items.item: Payment milestones show the due date, amount and status, with amounts right-aligned in tabular figures and formatted as currency, and the milestones are ordered with overdue and due-soon ones first
items.evidence: Amount cells use `${fmt(m.amount)}` (script around line 506) — currency-formatted via fmt() but left-aligned with no text-right/tabular-nums class. The `milestones` array (lines 480-486) is in delivery order, not overdue-first: the 'Overdue' milestone (due Mar 17, 2026) sits 5th, after three 'Paid' rows and even after an Oct 15, 2026 row, so overdue/due-soon items are not surfaced first.

items.item: Overdue or upcoming milestones are marked with a text label (such as "Overdue" or "Due in 5 days"), not by colour alone
items.evidence: Status badges render literal text via statusStyles/status, e.g. the Year 2 maintenance row renders `Overdue` and the closeout row renders 'Upcoming' — colour is paired with a text word, not used alone.

items.item: The renewal or expiry date is shown as an absolute date with the remaining time stated in words (such as "Expires in 45 days")
items.evidence: Expiration Date tile shows only the absolute date 'Mar 16, 2027' (line 81) with no accompanying 'Expires in N days' phrasing anywhere. The only countdown shown, 'Days to Renewal Decision: 41 days' (#daysToRenewal, line 85/519), is computed against the notice deadline (Dec 16, 2026), not the expiry date itself, so expiry has no stated remaining time in words.

items.item: Amendments are listed with number, date, a short summary and who approved them, using absolute dates
items.evidence: All four entries use absolute 'Effective <date>' text (e.g. 'Effective Sep 1, 2026', line 246) with numbers and summaries. But only Amendment No. 3 names approvers ('Approved by Legal (J. Nakamura) and Finance (A. Patel)', line 248); Amendment No. 2 and No. 1 (lines 255-269) give only a change summary with no approver attribution.

items.item: Each section has an empty state with a next action (such as "Add contact" or "Add amendment"), a loading state, and an inline error with retry
items.evidence: No loading placeholders, empty-state markup, or error/retry UI exists anywhere in the HTML or script — milestones/amendments/contacts are always rendered from hardcoded mock data (e.g. the `milestones` array, lines 479-486) with no alternate states; audit also reports loadingPlaceholders: 0.

items.item: Terminating the contract asks for confirmation that names the contract and the consequence, with a verb button label and focus not on the destructive button
items.evidence: No 'Terminate' action, button, or confirmation dialog exists anywhere in the markup or script. The only related control is the Renewal tab's 'Initiate Non-Renewal' button (line 340), which has no confirmation dialog attached and is a different action from termination.

tells:
initials-avatar-non-person — the vendor 'NB' tile (`
NB
`, line 353) uses a person-style initials avatar for a company, NorthBridge Networks Inc.
tracked-uppercase-labels — stat labels and section headers use `uppercase tracking-wide`, e.g. 'TOTAL CONTRACT VALUE' (line 72), 'CONTACTS' (line 374), 'PAID TO DATE' (line 224)
emoji-icon — document rows use the 📄 emoji (`📄`, lines 180/190) as a file-type icon and the vendor rating uses star glyphs '★★★★☆ 4.2' (line 370)

card-in-card — the blue 'Paid to Date / Remaining Balance' summary box (`bg-blue-50 border ... rounded-lg`, line 222) and the 'Renewal Checklist' box (`bg-white border ... rounded-lg`, line 312) are both nested inside the larger white bordered tab card
oversized-radius — outer cards use `rounded-xl` (12px), flagged by the audit's radius-scale violation (12px actual vs ≤8px expected) on `section.bg-white.rounded-xl`
notes: Core layout (tabs, breadcrumb, contact cards, amendment timeline) is well structured and the vendor-contact requirement fully passes, but several checklist items fail because the corresponding feature is simply absent (termination flow, section-level empty/loading/error states, vendor name in header) rather than mis-implemented. Milestone table formatting/ordering and amendment approver attribution are partially implemented but inconsistent.
